one_line: Shared architecture canvas for humans and AI agents.
what_it_does: Lets a human and agent inspect and mutate the same architecture diagram, including creating, connecting, arranging, reviewing, and persisting components.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to live canvas state and mutations, avoiding brittle visual manipulation and enabling human-agent shared-state work.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes agents inspecting, creating, connecting, arranging, and reviewing the same live canvas.
About text lists undo/redo, persistence, activity feed, import/export, and seven WebMCP capabilities.
execution_rationale: The frame sheet shows a coherent architecture-canvas interface and a configured user-query/agent workflow, but the visible frames do not clearly establish a complete end-to-end agent build.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows NodeCraft canvas, connected nodes, sidebar, and configuration/modal states.
About text describes a concrete central workflow and supporting state-management features.
impact_rationale: Architecture modeling is a credible developer workflow and shared state can reduce friction in collaborative design, though the demonstrated audience is specialized.
impact_evidence: Product targets architecture diagramming and collaborative review by developers and agents.
Shared live workspace addresses a concrete coordination problem.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-agent architecture canvas is a fresh, memorable interaction model with meaningful depth beyond a chat wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent edit one live diagram rather than maintaining separate representations.
Activity attribution and agent review are integrated into the canvas concept.
usability_note: Clear canvas metaphor and supporting controls; some configuration states appear unfinished in the frames.
red_flags: No transcript and no clearly visible completed tool result in the reviewed contact sheet.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-centered concept with credible product evidence and meaningful developer value.

one_line: Shared canvas that exposes hidden sauna-quote costs and buyer questions.
what_it_does: Turns a contractor quote into editable line items, scope risks, planning ranges, and questions for the seller, shared by buyer and agent.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared quote state lets an agent transform ambiguous scope into auditable line items and questions while the buyer corrects assumptions in place.
leverage_evidence: About text describes agent loading/structuring quote, human correction, rereading visible state, and question generation.
The product keeps the source of truth in the visible canvas rather than a separate chat.
execution_rationale: The stated reviewer-safe flow is unusually concrete: a quote total becomes a sourced range with missing scope exposed and questions generated; frames provide product-motion evidence, though details are small.
execution_evidence: About text gives a specific $11,750 to $12,250-$18,650 example.
Frame sheets show a quote-analysis canvas across sequential states.
impact_rationale: Home-improvement buyers face a real, costly information asymmetry, and surfacing electrical, foundation, permits, and other omissions has direct practical value.
impact_evidence: Specific buyer problem and hidden-cost categories are described.
Output includes actionable contractor questions, not just a generic summary.
creativity_rationale: Applying shared WebMCP state to quote diligence and negotiation preparation is a distinctive, well-motivated concept.
creativity_evidence: Quote becomes a collaborative decision canvas with explicit risks and sourced ranges.
Human authority over seller assumptions is built into the interaction model.
usability_note: Decision-canvas framing appears understandable and action-oriented.
red_flags: Agent invocation is described more clearly in text than in the small contact sheet.
standouts: Concrete, high-stakes example makes the value proposition legible.
advance_reason: Strong real-world use case, clear shared-state leverage, and concrete demonstrated outcome.

one_line: State-governed airline recovery simulation where the agent proposes and humans commit.
what_it_does: Uses dynamic WebMCP capability exposure to constrain recovery actions based on operational state, legality checks, and human approval.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic registration and withdrawal of consequential capabilities is central to the product; a general UI-driving agent cannot comparably rely on an authoritative state-governed tool surface.
leverage_evidence: About defines six operational states with different available capabilities.
cancel_flight disappears after violations resolve and commit_recovery_plan appears only at the proper state; committed mutation withdraws capabilities.
execution_rationale: The product presents a coherent deterministic simulation with visible state progression and approval gating; the frame sheet supports a functional control-desk workflow.
execution_evidence: About lists seven tools, legality checks, authorization, and six states.
Frame sheet shows operational simulation/task states progressing toward target completion.
impact_rationale: Airline disruption recovery is a credible high-stakes workflow where separating proposal from authority has clear safety and operational value.
impact_evidence: Scenario includes aircraft position, crew duty, minimum turn time, and disruption window constraints.
Human approval is required before committed schedule changes.
creativity_rationale: Treating the website's exposed capabilities as a dynamic authority boundary is a genuinely original WebMCP interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Capability existence itself changes with state and authorization.
The agent-proposes/site-decides/human-commits model is pursued through a concrete aviation testbed.
usability_note: State and authority model is explicit, though the operational simulation is specialized.
red_flags: Contact sheet does not expose readable tool traces, relying on packet description for invocation details.
advance_reason: Most compelling WebMCP leverage in the packet: dynamic authority is the product, not a convenience layer.

one_line: Agent-ready search for exact instructional lessons from natural-language questions.
what_it_does: Maps questions to approved teaching excerpts with lesson title, timestamps, citations, rationale, and controlled playback.
leverage_rationale: A structured search tool reliably returns authoritative lesson excerpts and timestamps, but a conventional search/chat integration could achieve much of the same outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: About describes learnlogos.search_training.v1 returning title, summary, timestamps, citation, and match explanation.
Shared validated search service powers both human interface and agent.
execution_rationale: Frames show a polished question-to-lesson flow with suggestions and an embedded result; agent invocation itself is not visibly established.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows question entry, autocomplete, submission, and lesson playback states.
About describes eight demonstrated alternative questions across two topics.
impact_rationale: Learners benefit from finding exact authoritative instruction when they remember a concept but not its course or terminology.
impact_evidence: Specific retrieval problem and timestamped/cited solution are clearly described.
Controlled playback and captions connect retrieval to learning.
creativity_rationale: The exact-lesson retrieval experience is useful and well executed but is a familiar semantic-search pattern.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language variants map to the same authoritative lesson.
Citation and timestamp integration add depth.
usability_note: The visible flow is clear: ask, select, watch.
red_flags: Frames show UI search rather than an explicit agent call.
standouts: Strong evidence of usable retrieval result.
advance_reason: Clear educational value and polished demonstrated workflow, despite moderate novelty and leverage.

one_line: Agent-addressable analytics and visualization for AI-transformation scores of S&P 500 companies.
what_it_does: Combines chart gallery, in-browser SQL, filters, and company reports to answer comparative questions about BATS scores.
leverage_rationale: Structured agent access can turn natural-language analytical questions into SQL and fitting charts, but the underlying dashboard remains usable through ordinary controls.
leverage_evidence: About explicitly positions WebMCP as a way for agents to drive the query surface rather than guess at clicks.
Product includes DuckDB SQL, chart selection, and linked company reports.
execution_rationale: The frame sheet clearly shows a functioning analytics dashboard and repeated chart states; packaging describes a broad but coherent set of views.
execution_evidence: Frames show BATS Visualization with ranked horizontal charts and controls.
About lists 25 chart cards, SQL tab, company detail navigation, and a demo query.
impact_rationale: Analysts and investors can compare sectors and companies more efficiently, though the use case is specialized and snapshot-based.
impact_evidence: Specific questions such as healthcare averages and industrials ranked by hype are identified.
Company reports and sector charts support analysis beyond a static table.
creativity_rationale: The synthesis of a score catalog, SQL, and charts is competent but belongs to a familiar analytics-dashboard pattern.
creativity_evidence: Agent-driven query-to-chart flow is a useful integration.
Frozen season snapshot and multiple visualization modes show scope.
usability_note: Dashboard and chart states are legible, though density may challenge first-time users.
red_flags: No explicit agent invocation visible in contact sheet; evidence is primarily dashboard output.
standouts: Good query-and-chart framing for an existing data catalog.
advance_reason: Solid analytical product with credible execution and meaningful, if not transformative, WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Multi-tenant expense manager exposing application actions and embedded WebMCP utilities.
what_it_does: Provides expenses, budgets, approvals, currencies, dashboards, agent tools, call history, and an embedded currency-conversion utility.
leverage_rationale: Mapping significant UI actions to real WebMCP tools and allowing an agent to coordinate expense and utility operations is useful, but most functions remain conventional CRUD.
leverage_evidence: About states each significant UI action corresponds to a document.modelContext tool.
Read-only tools include expense search, budget status, spend summary, and categories; embedded third-party utility is also WebMCP-enabled.
execution_rationale: Frames show expenses and dashboard surfaces with a coherent dark application shell; the packet describes broad functionality but not every workflow end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows expense list and dashboard/analytics states.
About lists organizations, roles, budgets, approval workflows, currencies, agent page, and call history.
impact_rationale: Expense tracking and approval workflows address a real business need, especially across currencies and roles.
impact_evidence: Product targets multi-tenant expense management with budgets and approvals.
Currency conversion and spend summaries are directly useful operations.
creativity_rationale: The cross-app WebMCP coordination angle is interesting, but expense management itself is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Embedded third-party utility and agent page extend the product beyond a simple expense list.
Tool-per-action contract is systematically applied.
usability_note: Rich feature set is visible, though density and multi-surface scope add complexity.
red_flags: Broad claimed scope exceeds what the contact sheet alone can verify.
advance_reason: Credible business utility and substantial implementation breadth, with moderate novelty.

one_line: Human-sealed reading desk for agent-assisted uncertain handwriting transcription.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect handwriting, compare evidence, propose readings, and collaborate without silently overwriting human decisions; stale revisions are rejected.
leverage_rationale: Shared evidence state, human sealing, revision safety, and stale-proposal rejection make WebMCP central to trustworthy agent-human transcription.
leverage_evidence: About describes eight tools, visible evidence, human-only accept/reject/illegible decisions, and STALE_REVISION protection.
Final export records decisions, revisions, and a SHA-256 integrity hash.
execution_rationale: Frames show a deliberately designed reading desk, evidence lens, receipts, and stale-revision safety sequence; the product scope is coherent and clearly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet visibly includes reading desk, evidence lens, collaboration receipts, and stale-revision sections.
About gives a synthetic ledger with three unclear words and a complete investigation loop.
impact_rationale: Historical and archival transcription has a real accuracy problem where a confident wrong reading can cause lasting harm; the workflow directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Specific audience/problem: researchers handling faded, damaged, or ambiguous historical records.
Evidence presentation and human final authority address reliability concerns.
creativity_rationale: The evidence-first, human-sealed transcription desk and stale revision protocol are highly original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Evidence Lens exposes competing readings rather than only a guessed output.
Receipts, revision safety, and integrity hash make the interaction model memorable.
usability_note: The reading-desk metaphor and evidence panels support careful review, though the workflow is specialized.
red_flags: Synthetic ledger limits claims about real archival deployment.
standouts: Exceptional evidence and concurrency safety treatment.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-integrity WebMCP use with strong visual and textual evidence.

one_line: Controlled bridge from WebMCP agents to observed and approved desktop actions.
what_it_does: Combines screen observation, structured proposals, policy checks, human approval, bounded local execution, verification, logs, and reusable workflows.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP acts as the structured control plane for software outside the browser, with explicit approval and post-action verification; this is materially beyond UI button driving.
leverage_evidence: About defines Observe → Propose → Approve → Act → Verify and a bounded native companion.
Tools cover observation, target resolution, policy, approvals, execution, verification, events, and workflows.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent safety-oriented control loop and deterministic Paint, Notepad, and Claims demonstrations; contact-sheet invocation evidence was unavailable, so confidence is slightly reduced.
execution_evidence: About lists inspectable event timeline, reusable workflows, verification, and bounded bridge.
Frame sheet was not successfully analyzed after retries; textual packet evidence is strong.
impact_rationale: A controlled agent interface for legacy, creative, enterprise, and desktop software addresses a broad and concrete automation gap.
impact_evidence: Product explicitly targets desktop apps, legacy enterprise tools, creative software, games, and testing environments.
Approval and verification reduce risks of blind macros.
creativity_rationale: Extending WebMCP beyond webpages through a bounded, inspectable desktop bridge is ambitious and conceptually original.
creativity_evidence: Combines screen observation with structured proposals and policy checks.
Per-step approval and post-action verification are a distinctive interaction model.
usability_note: Safety stages are explicit, but the bridge setup and policy model may add user friction.
red_flags: Image analysis failed after retries, so video evidence is unclear and confidence is capped.
advance_reason: Very strong concept and packet description; visual verification is incomplete due to image-analysis failure.

one_line: Proof-carrying WebMCP delegation with dynamic approval-gated capabilities.
what_it_does: Defines mission envelopes, evidence and policy checks, stages reversible actions, exposes commit only after human approval, and verifies cryptographic receipts.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic capability exposure is the core product: consequential authority literally appears only after a human decision and disappears after commit.
leverage_evidence: About describes seven tools initially, an eighth commit tool after approval, then unregistering after action.
Mission, evidence, policy, receipt verification, and audit export are structured WebMCP operations.
execution_rationale: The packet specifies a complete synthetic release flow with threshold breach, approval, commit, receipt recomputation, and attribution; frames support a staged control-plane demo.
execution_evidence: About gives concrete $1,840 action, $1,000 approval threshold, approval transition, commit, and SHA-256 receipt verification.
Frame sheet is listed as product-motion evidence across three sheets.
impact_rationale: Delegated actions with spending ceilings, evidence, and receipts address a real trust and governance problem for agent automation.
impact_evidence: Mission envelopes and audit bundles target consequential workflows.
Human, agent, and policy-engine attribution makes accountability explicit.
creativity_rationale: Proof-carrying delegation and capability appearance/disappearance form a novel, ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Commit capability is absent until visible approval.
Cryptographic receipt and independent verification deepen the concept beyond approval UX.
usability_note: The approval and receipt states are explicit, though the governance model is more complex than ordinary task apps.
red_flags: All demo data is synthetic and no real payment API is connected.
standouts: Excellent end-to-end authority and audit model.
advance_reason: Top-tier WebMCP leverage with concrete state transitions, safety, and verification.

one_line: Agent-driven YouTube transcript and explainer-slide tool for cutting through video noise.
what_it_does: Fetches timestamped captions for a YouTube URL and renders agent-authored explanatory slides with timestamp links and read-aloud playback.
leverage_rationale: Structured transcript retrieval and rendering reduce friction for an agent, but a general agent with transcript access could reproduce much of the outcome.
leverage_evidence: About names get_transcript(url) and render_explainer(slides,url) with schemas and structured errors.
Rendered timestamps link back to video moments and the same result can be produced through a manual render box.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a compact complete flow and the contact sheet shows processing/result states, but detailed end-to-end agent interaction is not clearly visible.
execution_evidence: About describes caption retrieval, timestamped segments, slide rendering, and read-aloud.
Frame sheet shows a processing-to-result progression for the single-page tool.
impact_rationale: People who need to extract signal from long YouTube videos have a clear, common problem and receive navigable summaries.
impact_evidence: Product directly targets long-video noise and timestamped comprehension.
Read-aloud and timestamp links improve accessibility and follow-up.
creativity_rationale: Transcript-plus-explainer is a familiar category, but agent-authored timestamped slides and explicit failure semantics add a useful angle.
creativity_evidence: Render tool turns agent output into a navigable visual explainer.
Three-way measurement/error outcomes show thoughtful implementation detail.
usability_note: Simple paste-link workflow is accessible; generated explainer quality depends on the agent.
red_flags: The contact sheet does not clearly expose tool-call UI or agent identity.
standouts: Good timestamp-linked output and honest error-state design.
advance_reason: Useful, coherent product with modest novelty and leverage but credible execution.
